title.narrative: EEPSEA - Environmental Economics Program in South East Asia 2012-2016

description.narrative: EEPSEA is a regional network that seeks to strengthen capacity in the area of poverty, economic development and environmental change by strengthen the ability of researchers in Southeast Asia to undertake policy relevant research, support the growth of rigorous policy-relevant literature, support teaching/research insitutions and by facilitate dialoge among economist and others on environment

EEPSEA är ett regionalt forskningsnätverk som strävar efter att stärka kapaciteten för forskning som rör fattigdom, ekonomisk utveckling och miljö. Syftet är att stärka sydostasiatiska forskares förmåga att bedriva policy-relevant forskning, stärka framväxten av rigorös policy-relevant literatur, stödja undervisnings- och forskningsinstitutioner, samt underlätta dialogen mellen ekonomer och
Improved design and implementation of policies and programs towards sustainable environmental and natural resource management.

EEPSEA built environmental economics (EE) research capacity in the Southeast Asia region by offering training courses, awarding research grants, and providing research mentoring support. The program aimed at increasing the analytical capacity of local researchers from national and regional institutions, particularly in dealing with environmental issues. The programme also contributed towards increasing the number of researchers doing EE research in the region and worked towards increasing the probability that such economic analyses are considered in environmental and natural resource management and policymaking. On an output level EEPSEA achieved all expected results and the quality is assessed to have been high. EEPSEA held 34 training courses for researchers from all over the region, 21 were regional courses and 13 were in-country courses. The 34 courses were attended by 833 researchers from all over the region. The majority of the training participants (75%) are university-based researchers/lecturers who teach undergraduate and graduate courses. EEPSEA also trained 292 non-traditional research users like policymakers, natural resource managers, and green bench justices. EEPSEA awarded 88 research grants involving 229 researchers. Of the 229 researchers, 34 were involved in cross-country research projects. 57% of the research grantees were women. Most research projects focused on understanding the root cause of environmental problems (74%), the other 37% considered the poverty dimension and the gender aspect. A total of 177 publications were produced. Several programme alumni reported that they have been approached for advice policy makers and that their EEPSEA training supports their teaching. Further, at least 37 universities have ENRE courses or with courses that incorporated an ENRE module that been influenced by EEPSEA. The programme also facilitated the building of an organisation that aims to continue its legacy of environmental economics research capacity building in the region, the Economy and Environment Partnership for South East Asia (EEPSEA Partnership).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
